title: A workflow event, version 1
description: One line of the bridge's local friction log: where work got stuck, for how long, and on whom. docs/workflow-event.md explains it. A new version is a new file; this one is never edited once published.

v.description: The format's version, written first. A reader skips and counts a version it does not read.

at.description: When the bridge wrote the event, to the second, with its offset.

source.description: The registered name of the collector that saw it, set by the bridge.

id.description: Stable per friction point: the source, the collector's own key and the friction's start to the second, in UTC. An open and its close share it.

session.description: The session, from the bridge's programme files, never from what the collector read.

repo.description: The repository, from the bridge's programme files, never from what the collector read.

kind.description: What sort of friction it is.

blocker.description: Who or what it waits on. owner is the owner; roy is its old name, still written by older bridges and kept in old lines, and read as owner.

state.description: open when it is seen, closed when it ends, or point for one moment with no duration.

started.description: When the friction began, with its offset. A point starts when it is written.

duration_s.description: Only on a close: at minus started, in whole seconds. Null otherwise.

what.description: A path the repository's git knows, a rule name, or a word from the collector's own vocabulary. Anything else is the collector's catch-all word, or null when it has none.

line.description: One line, kept in the local log only, after the private scan and with token-shaped text blanked. Null when there is none or it held private data.

closed_late.description: Only on a close the bridge saw after the friction had ended while it was down. Its at is when it looked, so the duration is at most that.
